sources.title: Introducing computer use, a new Claude 3.5 Sonnet, and Claude 3.5 Haiku
sources.evidence: October 22, 2024 announcement names Claude 3.5 Haiku, describes low latency, coding, tool use and specialized sub-agent uses, and says public availability was still forthcoming. Reopened October 27: performance similarity to Claude 3 Opus and previous Haiku does not identify a sized base model or nominal count.

sources.title: Claude Platform release notes
sources.evidence: November 4, 2024 entry announces text-only API availability; February 24, 2025 adds vision. February 19, 2026 entry explicitly maps Claude Haiku 3.5 to claude-3-5-haiku-20241022 and records its retirement on the Claude API.

sources.title: Model Card Addendum: Claude 3.5 Haiku and Upgraded Claude 3.5 Sonnet
sources.evidence: Original model-card addendum identifies Haiku 3.5 as a Claude 3-family model and reports tool-use, coding and reasoning evaluations. Its technical text and comparison tables provide no total/active parameter counts or dense/MoE architecture specification. Fresh inspection used the same October addendum in Anthropic's combined Claude 3 card (s11), including Introduction and Table 8.

sources.title: Partner model deprecations — Claude 3.5 Haiku on Google Cloud
sources.evidence: Exact Claude 3.5 Haiku section documents 200,000-token context, text/code/image input, text output, function calling, no extended thinking, and a documents specification pointing to PDF support. Its release-date row says October 22, conflicting with explicit availability announcements; treated as snapshot/announcement date. Retained deprecated-model specifications do not prove current operation.

sources.title: Unsupervised Elicitation of Language Models
sources.evidence: Section 3.3 explicitly classifies Claude 3.5 Haiku and Claude 3 Haiku as proprietary, contrasting them with open-weight Llama models. Experiments largely use pretrained variants; section 4.4 separately discusses the publicly released Claude 3.5 Haiku assistant. This establishes classification, not parameter counts or a named weight license. Reopened October 27: section 3.3 assigns the 8B and 70B sizes to Llama 3.1, not Haiku. Section 4.4 distinguishes experimental Haiku-based assistants from public Claude 3.5 Haiku; neither its pretrained base nor public assistant receives a size.

sources.title: System Card: Claude Haiku 4.5
sources.evidence: October 2025 successor card explicitly identifies Claude Haiku 3.5 as the previous Haiku model and states it had no extended-thinking mode. Exact-name comparison tables report evaluations, not parameter counts; searched text provides no parameter-count or architecture specification for Haiku 3.5. Fresh PDF retrieved October 27 at 10:11:46 UTC: section 1.1.2 and exact-name tables, including Table 2.1.1.A, describe modes and evaluation rates, with no nominal total or activated-parameter column.

sources.title: Announcing Anthropic’s upgraded Claude 3.5 Sonnet and Claude 3.5 Haiku on Vertex AI
sources.evidence: Editor's note explicitly distinguishes October 22 pre-announcement from the November 4, 2024 update confirming Haiku 3.5 availability.

sources.title: Claude 3.7 Sonnet System Card
sources.evidence: Later first-party system card reviewed as an additional disclosure check. It introduces extended thinking for Sonnet 3.7; no total/active parameter count or architecture specification for Haiku 3.5 was found in its parsed text. Fresh PDF retrieved October 27 at 10:08:59 UTC from https://www-cdn.anthropic.com/9ff93dfa8f445c932415d335c88852ef47f1201e.pdf was rechecked for total/active counts and named sized lineage; none supports Haiku 3.5.

sources.title: On the Biology of a Large Language Model
sources.evidence: March 27, 2025 first-party research explicitly studies production Claude 3.5 Haiku. Method Overview says the studied models are Transformer-based, with MLP and attention layers. The 30 million features describe its replacement transcoder, not the production model parameter count; no total/active count or dense/MoE designation is established. Reopened October 27 and followed its companion methods paper (s12), which separately identifies the smaller 18-layer research model.

sources.title: Claude Model Pricing — List Prices by Platform, effective May 12, 2026
sources.evidence: Parent reviewed page3: the May12,2026 API pricing table lists 200K and 1M rows for Claude 3.5 Haiku. These rows postdate Anthropic API retirement and conflict with retained exact-model context specifications; no corroborating availability announcement was found.

sources.title: The Claude 3 Model Family: Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, with June and October 2024 addenda
sources.evidence: Fresh official PDF retrieved 2026-10-27T10:09:00.971358+00:00 and inspected from its extracted text. October addendum Introduction calls Haiku 3.5 a new Claude 3-family model; Table 8 compares benchmark scores. Neither supplies nominal total/active parameters or an explicit relationship to a named model with a published size. The original family card's relative parameter-scaling statement concerns Claude 3 Haiku through Opus and provides no numeric count.

sources.title: Circuit Tracing: Revealing Computational Graphs in Language Models
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27. Training discussion distinguishes the small 18-layer research transformer from Claude 3.5 Haiku. The 300K-30M Haiku quantities count features in cross-layer transcoders trained to replace its MLPs, not the underlying language model's parameters. No nominal total or active count is given.

sources.title: Claude 3.5 Haiku on AWS Trainium2 and model distillation in Amazon Bedrock
sources.evidence: December 3, 2024 developer post reopened October 27 through its original anthropic.com/news URL. It describes latency-optimized Claude 3.5 Haiku inference separately from distillation of Claude 3.5 Sonnet into Claude 3 Haiku. This is not a statement that Claude 3.5 Haiku is a variant of a sized base model; no parameter count is published.

sources.title: System Card: Claude Haiku 5.5, October 7, 2026
sources.evidence: Latest Haiku card fetched 2026-10-27T10:11:48.624710+00:00. Fresh text review of training and comparison material found no retrospective Haiku 3.5 total or activated-parameter specification, nor a named sized-base relationship. Its predecessor comparisons concern Haiku 4.5 and do not establish Haiku 3.5 size.

name.note: Current official naming order; launch materials also use Claude 3.5 Haiku.

developer.note: Developer-authored announcement and card identify Anthropic.

family.note: Normalized catalog family key for Anthropic's Haiku model line; the original card also places it within the broader Claude 3 generation.

release_date.note: Earliest public availability verified by Anthropic's own dated API release entry and Google's availability update. October 22 is the announcement/model snapshot date, despite the conflicting date in Google's later specifications table.

open_weights.note: Anthropic-authored research explicitly distinguishes Claude 3.5 Haiku as proprietary from open-weight Llama models. Paid API access alone is not used as the evidence.

license.note: Descriptive proprietary classification explicitly supported by Anthropic research. The catalog permits this category; it does not imply an SPDX or public weight-distribution license.

parameters_b.note: Fresh October 27 nominal-size search found no developer-published total or explicit lineage to a named model with a published count. Rechecked the original October addendum, later cards and exact-model research. The elicitation paper's 8B/70B counts belong to Llama; the circuit-tracing study's 18-layer model and 30M transcoder features are distinct from production Haiku 3.5. The Trainium2 post distills into Claude 3 Haiku, not Haiku 3.5. Performance comparisons and family succession do not establish a count.

active_parameters_b.note: Separately rechecked active/activated parameters in the original card, exact-name Haiku 4.5 comparison tables, later Haiku 5.5 card and interpretability research. No active-parameter specification or comparison column was found. Sparse transcoder feature activity does not measure production-model active parameters; no total-to-active equality or dense/MoE routing is inferred.

architecture.note: The exact-model interpretability study explicitly describes Transformer-based models with MLP and attention layers. Dense/MoE routing and parameter counts remain undisclosed; replacement-transcoder features are not model parameters.

context_window.note: Provider's retained exact-model specifications state 200,000 context length; this is a documented model limit, not a current endpoint-operation test. A later post-retirement pricing table also lists a conflicting 1M API tier; retain 200K from exact-model documentation because the pricing row does not establish feature availability.

modalities.note: Initially text-only; Anthropic added image input on February 24, 2025. Google's exact-model technical table documents images and PDF documents; PDF denotes supported document processing, not a separate learned sensory modality. This records later documented capability.

reasoning.note: False means no dedicated extended-thinking mode. The later Haiku 4.5 card explicitly confirms this for Haiku 3.5; it does not mean the model cannot solve reasoning tasks.

tool_call.note: Anthropic describes improved tool use; the exact-model provider specification lists function calling.

description.value: Claude Haiku model released in November 2024 with a 200K-token context window and tool calling.
description.note: Plain description of verified release, context and tool support.

patch.notes: Announced October 22, 2024; Anthropic's release notes confirm public API availability November 4. Image input was added February 24, 2025, so modalities describe later documented capability. No extended-thinking mode. Transformer architecture is documented by Anthropic interpretability research; nominal total/active counts and dense/MoE routing remain undisclosed. The study's 30M features belong to a replacement transcoder. Claude API retirement was February 19, 2026; retained capability documentation does not establish current endpoint availability. A May 12, 2026 pricing PDF lists a conflicting 1M API tier after retirement; retained exact-model specifications support 200K.

summary: Fresh October 27 parameter re-audit retains null/undisclosed nominal total and active counts after reopening original evidence, inspecting later first-party comparisons and resolving base-model, distillation and interpretability leads. No published sized lineage was established. Explicit null patch and concise parameter clarification added; unrelated audited fields are unchanged.

parameter_reaudit.outcome: No supported nominal total or active count; primary lineage leads are unsized and research-feature counts do not describe the production model.
